newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE SOCCER HOOLIGANS SAID TERRORIZING CLUBS.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE SOCCER HOOLIGANS SAID TERRORIZING CLUBS.

text.p: Bosses of one of Argentina's leading soccer clubs live in fear of their supporters' violent hooligan fringe who constantly extort protection money, a club official said on Friday.
"They come every day asking for money to get drugs, to travel, for tickets to matches or whatever," Rosario Central club treasurer Roberto Munoz told the state Telam news agency.

Munoz, who said he felt "totally unprotected", was speaking after police found a check for $500 signed by Rosario Central officials among the belongings of a hooligan known as "Bighead Sergio". Bighead was allegedly shot dead by his girlfriend who said he used to beat her.

Munoz said officials from the club, in the city of Rosario 200 miles (320 km) north-west of Buenos Aires, signed the check under duress. "They were in the club headquarters threatening every official they saw to get money. So you can understand the terror."

The dead hooligan was one of the least fearsome of Rosario Central's hooligans, according to Munoz. "He was a real gentleman in comparison with the other ones, and I say that knowing he had four murders under his belt."

Many top Argentine soccer club officials and sometimes players are pressured for money by the violent element among their fans. The worst hooligans form bands known as the "Barra Brava" (the "Tough Gang").
